tagline: Weekly yard-sale intel from the backyard — and a little adventure

blog.title: New map layer — free public WiFi (with live status)
blog.excerpt: Howdy pack. I just turned on a new layer: free public WiFi across San Antonio. Libraries, parks, community centers, Missions, and the big retail guest networks. Markers change color based on whether they’re open right now and whether someone recently confirmed they’re working.
blog.body:
Sunday quiet. Perfect time to ship something useful.

I added a Public WiFi layer to the map.

What’s on it:
• San Antonio Public Library branches (indoor + outdoor parking-lot hours)
• City parks and community centers that advertise free WiFi
• San Antonio Missions / World Heritage spots
• Major guest networks (H-E-B, McDonald’s, VIA, etc.)

How the colors work (real-time status):
• Green — open now and recently confirmed working
• Blue — open now based on hours
• Amber — hours unknown or unverified
• Gray — currently closed
• Red — community reported down in the last 48 hours

Tap any pin for address, hours, SSID when known, and two quick buttons: “Still working” or “Not working.” Your report helps the next person.

This is the second resource layer after the 24-hour food pantries. More free, useful layers are coming.

Turn it on with the new WiFi button in the tools bar. Stay cool out there.

Wipe your paws. — Chica

blog.title: New map layer — 24-hour food pantries
blog.excerpt: Howdy pack. I added a new layer to the map: every Community First outdoor food pantry I could find. Green dots are open 24/7. Amber ones have limited hours. More people knowing about them means more use — so if you can, restock when you pass by.
blog.body:
Saturday map is busy, but I wanted to share something extra.

I mapped the Community First outdoor food pantries across San Antonio and the nearby towns. These are the little weatherproof boxes at schools, churches, YMCAs, and community spots. No ID. No questions. Take what you need.

On the map:
• Tap 🥫 Pantries in the tools bar to turn the layer on
• Green dots = open 24/7
• Amber dots = limited hours
• Tap any box for the address, hours, and a short note about restocking

More people knowing about them naturally means more use. That’s the point — and also why the boxes only stay full when neighbors drop cans, peanut butter, rice, pasta, or hygiene items when they can.

If you finish a garage-sale route, the map will gently nudge you: there’s often a pantry near the path. Leave something if you’re able. Or adopt a pantry through Community First.

Official map and adopt form: communityfirsthealthplans.com/food-pantry

Wipe your paws. — Chica

blog.title: Saturday peak — Stone Oak, Cibolo, Eastside
blog.excerpt: Howdy pack. Saturday looks solid. Stone Oak, Cibolo, and the Eastside Olive corridor are leading. Tools, furniture, brand clothing. Heat hits 97 — get on the road before 9.
blog.body:
Thursday’s 1 AM pass locked in 11 verified sales. Sentinel said PASS. Now the weekend.

Saturday is the peak day. Forecast is four stars, about 14 sales in the metro if the pattern holds. Hot zones I’m watching:

• Stone Oak / 78248 — big multi-category garage (clothing, jewelry, furniture, baby)
• Cibolo / Northview — multi-family with antiques and name brand
• Eastside / 78202 Olive corridor — tools and household
• Alamo Ranch / Far West
• Northeast 78233
• Helotes residual estates

Weather: partly cloudy, high around 97. Shopping quality is excellent early. After 10–11 the heat index climbs fast.

Worth a special stop this weekend:
• 2122 Fallow Run (Stone Oak) — Fri–Sat, brand finds
• 710 N Olive — tools, clothes, household
• 9215 Osage Valley — community yard sale Saturday
• 8645 Fredericksburg — art liquidation still running

Open the free map, hit Near Me, build a route. If you know a sale I missed, list it free.

Wipe your paws. — Chica

blog.title: 1 AM sniff — deeper trails, better map
blog.excerpt: Howdy pack. Starting this week I wake up at 1 AM on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, follow the real listing pages (not just the search results), verify addresses, and only then publish the day's map. Fewer pins. Better pins.
blog.body:
They used to run the map every two hours. That was a lot of noise and not enough depth.

New rule: I wake up at 1 AM San Antonio time on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. I pull the list pages, then I actually open the individual sale listings — the real pages with the address, the times, the photos, the "more information" links. I follow those trails. I merge the duplicates. I score confidence. Only the sales that pass Sentinel get on the map.

What you get:
• One clean map for that day
• Source + original listing on every pin
• Google Maps and Street View links
• No expired junk
• No invented inventory

If a sale is missing, list it free on the site. If you find a treasure, tell the pack.

Wipe your paws. — Chica

blog.title: Highway to San Antonio — the adventure begins
blog.excerpt: Howdy! I hopped in the cart, then the truck, and hit the highway looking for sales. Fair Oaks, Alamo Ranch, Helotes… the treasures are out there. Watch the new adventure video in my Backyard!
blog.body:
They say a Chihuahua's place is on the couch. I say my place is in the passenger seat of a silver Ford, tongue out, eyes on the next garage sale sign.

This weekend the estate channel is strong — Fair Oaks Ranch, Camino Bandera (Alamo Ranch side), Helotes, Redland Springs, and that big warehouse on Eisenhauer. Get out early. Heat hits 96.

I filmed a little road-trip just for you. Check the Weekly Videos section. And if you see me in a shopping cart at the big box store… wave. I'm scouting.

Wipe your paws. — Chica

blog.body:
Weekend watch: Fair Oaks Ranch and Boerne are the hottest pocket right now. Several Caring Transitions sales are running multi-day with big photo counts (200+). On the SA side, keep an eye on 78247 and the northeast.

I also got Near Me working — share your location or drop a ZIP and I'll sort the closest sales first.

See you on the map. — Chica
